lead: >-
  Gastronomic experiences are unevenly distributed throughout this trip:
  a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires is included, while the wineries
  of Chile's Maipo Valley can be visited for an additional fee. The Bolivian
  and Peruvian stages focus primarily on Andean nature and historical monuments.

## What gastronomic experiences are actually included in this four-country trip?

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a food and wine theme across Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru. Its basis is a [20-day group journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). The four countries in the title form part of an itinerary that also includes Brazil and Uruguay. This journey covers more than four nations.

There are two gastronomic experiences on the itinerary, with different conditions: a [tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/) and the option of visiting [Maipo Valley wineries](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) for a tasting. **The wine excursion is optional and costs extra.** This is an important distinction from the included dinner. No standalone culinary workshops or tasting tours are specified in the published itinerary for Bolivia or Peru.

## How the four stages differ

| Country | Confirmed activity |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Dinner during a tango show |
| Chile | Wine tasting, at an additional cost |
| Bolivia | Uyuni and high-altitude lagoons |
| Peru | Cusco and Machu Picchu |

**Argentina.** After sightseeing in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), travelers attend a tango show with dinner. This combines an evening performance and a meal; it is not a series of restaurant tastings around the country. The inclusion of a [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/) does not imply a separate cooking class.

**Chile.** A trip from [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is possible. This wine-growing region is known for vineyards and tasting programs. However, the main tour day is occupied by sightseeing in Santiago: an optional winery visit must be agreed in advance in terms of timing, content and payment. If wine matters more than the number of countries visited, compare [food and wine tours in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/).

**Bolivia.** After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), an off-road itinerary begins through lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Certain sections are over 4,000 meters above sea level, with an expedition-style overnight stay. The main considerations here are coping with altitude, weather and vehicle transfers. The confirmed program has no additional gastronomic day.

**Peru.** The tour passes Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) before reaching Lima. These stops are primarily devoted to Andean culture and history. A separate food excursion in Peru should not be assumed to be included simply because the entire journey appears in this thematic catalog.

## When to make time for a wine excursion

The itinerary travels through Buenos Aires and Santiago **before** ascending into high-altitude Bolivia. The day after Santiago includes a flight to Calama and a drive into the Atacama, followed by a two-day jeep tour. This explains why a winery day needs to be planned in advance: the length of the outing affects city sightseeing, rest before the flight and the subsequent schedule.

Ada Tours helps coordinate optional activities, transportation and the order of visits. The specific winery, tasting contents and booking conditions are confirmed separately. If you want a multi-day wine journey involving several regions and producers, the published 20-day program has a different priority: a long route from the Atlantic to the Andes.

The [general Argentina–Bolivia–Chile–Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_chile_peru/) addresses a different set of questions: distances, flights, borders and the choice of all tours. Here, the key factor is the actual place of food and wine experiences within the journey.

## Comparing the itinerary and the price

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

The main tour and the optional wine excursion are separate services with separate costs. Before choosing, clarify your interest in Maipo, the sequence of domestic flights and your readiness for the high-altitude Bolivian stage. For a broader introduction to this type of travel, visit [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/); the particular tour determines the conditions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the Maipo wine tasting already included in the price?

No. The current itinerary lists the [Maipo Valley wineries](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) as an excursion charged separately. The visit and its conditions must be arranged individually.

### Are there cooking workshops in Bolivia and Peru?

The published itinerary does not include standalone cooking workshops in those countries. The Bolivian stage passes lagoons and Uyuni; the Peruvian stage covers Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

### Can I visit only the four named countries?

This catalog includes programs passing through each of these four countries, but the [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also visits Brazil and Uruguay. A shorter, customized itinerary would need separate arrangements.

  Atacama, Bolivia's colored lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca.
  Longer tours continue to Cusco and Machu Picchu and also visit Brazil and
  other countries. The main question is how to balance altitude and time
  outdoors with a busy cultural itinerary.

## From Iguazu Falls to the Atacama Desert and Lake Titicaca

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose principal destinations include [Argentina](/argentina/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/). All these itineraries also visit Brazil; the filter does not promise a standalone tour of strictly the selected four countries. The [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) illustrates the core route, the [20-day program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds Uruguay, and the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues farther across the continent.

Choose this selection for its dramatic changes in scenery. On Argentina's border with Brazil, nature is humid and subtropical; in Chile there are dry mountain deserts; Bolivia offers high-altitude lagoons and salt flats; Peru has a highland lake and green slopes around Machu Picchu. Do not confuse the natural highlights with an assumption that every day is devoted to hiking: a substantial portion of the journey involves cities, transfers and historical landmarks.

## Argentina: Iguazu rather than Patagonia

The principal Argentine nature stop on the current itineraries is [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), near the Brazilian border. The 32-day program specifically includes [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/). An extensive waterfall system lies amid subtropical forest. UNESCO recognizes the neighboring Argentine and Brazilian national parks for their outstanding natural significance.

These particular tours **do not have a required Patagonia nature stage**. Travelers should not expect glaciers, Torres del Paine or Tierra del Fuego just because Argentina appears in the filter. The itineraries also cover Buenos Aires and other cultural destinations. Choosing Argentina in this catalog primarily means excursions to Iguazu.

For a fuller view of different Argentine regions, browse [nature tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) rather than imagining additional stops in a specific program.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as the gateway to high-altitude Bolivia

The Chilean stage centers on [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the transition from Chilean desert landscapes to Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and salt flats. The contrast with Iguazu is dramatic: dry air, open mountain spaces and bright sunlight replace humid forest.

All six programs pass through this area, but **mentioning Atacama does not make every well-known excursion in the region an included activity**. Visits to the Atacama Salt Flat, the Valley of the Moon or the El Tatio geysers must be checked in the chosen tour's own itinerary, not assumed from a general description of the region.

What matters most is the actual sequence: Chile forms the necessary link between the lower-altitude early stages and the Bolivian highlands. This affects both clothing choices and how travelers pace themselves.

## Bolivia: lagoons, geysers and the salt flat

The main highland sights are [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Even within one country, they offer very different landscapes: colorful mineral lakes, a geothermal area, stony terrain and a vast salt plain.

Uyuni is particularly dependent on the weather. When water covers the surface, a mirror effect may appear; at other times, the characteristic salt-crust patterns are visible. These are natural seasonal variations, not two separate tourism products. The colors and appearance of the lagoons also vary with the light and environmental conditions.

For every option, ask the organizer in advance how many hours will be spent in vehicles on the Bolivian stage and where the overnight stays take place. This is high-altitude travel; the climate is different from Argentina's tropical areas, and distances between stops can feel longer than they look on a map.

## Peru: Titicaca and the mountain scenery of Machu Picchu

Peru continues the high-altitude route through [Lake Titicaca near Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). A boat excursion on Titicaca offers views of island settlements and surrounding mountains. Around Machu Picchu, the vegetation changes: the ancient Inca structures stand among steep green slopes.

UNESCO recognizes both the cultural and natural value of the Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu. However, an admission ticket and guided visit to the archaeological site are not the same as an independent trek in the neighboring mountains. If an athletic route is the priority, it must be expressly included in the chosen program.

## What to consider when choosing the duration

| What to compare | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Which sides of the falls and the border crossing |
| San Pedro | Start of the high-altitude stage |
| Bolivian lagoons | Roads, altitude and cold |
| Uyuni | Season and actual route |
| Titicaca | Boat days and transfers |
| Machu Picchu | Time, tickets and visit format |

An extended South American tour passes through very different climates: humid Iguazu, the dry Atacama plateau, cold high-altitude parts of Bolivia and Peru's Andean valleys. Clothing for one region will not suit all the others. Do not estimate the time available for outdoor walks from the country names alone; compare each day's program, the number of transfers and the included excursions.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [full Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_chile_peru/) presents the same countries without a nature filter. Find further options among [multi-country nature tours](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru

### Is Patagonia included in these programs?

No. The confirmed nature days in Argentina are primarily associated with [Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Visiting Patagonia requires a different itinerary that explicitly lists the destinations.

### Do the tours include every Atacama excursion?

No. The current itineraries include [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and onward travel to Bolivia. Other activities in the region cannot be assumed to be included without explicit confirmation.

### What is Bolivia's most characteristic natural attraction?

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is one of the principal attractions, but [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the Sol de Mañana geothermal area are also significant. Assess the variety of the Bolivian stage across all its days rather than from one photograph of the salt flat.

### Is the mirror effect at Uyuni guaranteed?

No. Reflections require water on the salt surface. Weather and season determine how the landscape looks.

### Is Machu Picchu included as a trekking activity?

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is listed as a visit to a historic site. A separate multi-day trek should not be assumed unless it is specifically included in the program.

## Where to watch wildlife on a trip through Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru

**At Iguazu the waterfalls are the main attraction, while flamingos may be seen at the Bolivian lagoons.** Near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walkways run through forest toward the cascades and Devil's Throat. In Bolivia, travelers cross the plateau in off-road vehicles and stop at lagoons and the salt flat. Capitals, historic cities and travel days lie between these stages.

The catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a “Wildlife and Safaris” theme whose main countries include Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru. **This is an intersection of countries, not a ready-made continuous trip confined to just four of them.** The corresponding itineraries also include Brazil, while some continue through Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia. The full selection without the nature filter is available in the [four-country catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_chile_peru/).

## Argentina: Iguazu's forests and water

On the Argentine side of the falls, designated walkways take visitors close to individual cascades. This is a walking excursion through a protected natural area. The main experience is **seeing the falls up close and walking forest trails**, not a guaranteed encounter with particular animals.

The same trips generally include the [Brazilian side of Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). It offers a broad panorama of the cascades, while the Argentine side reveals other sections of the waterfall system. Brazil is absent from this selection's title but is included in the actual multi-country tours.

Each side has its own national-park entrance. The border crossing, admission conditions and walking times need to be coordinated: touring one bank does not automatically replace visiting the other. A general sightseeing excursion is not equivalent to a dedicated wildlife-watching trip.

## Chile: the Atacama Desert as a transition to the highlands

[San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) serves as the starting point for onward travel to Bolivia's lagoons. The programs include a flight to Calama and a ground transfer, followed by time to adapt before the higher-altitude stages. Chile offers arid plains and volcanic landscapes, very different from Iguazu's humid forest.

**The “Wildlife and Safaris” thematic label does not imply a dedicated wildlife excursion in the Atacama.** On these routes, San Pedro chiefly provides the geography and logistics of the transition to the Bolivian plateau. An astronomical outing, if offered, may be optional and is a different type of observation.

The large altitude difference between earlier lowland cities and the Andean highlands has practical implications. Discuss the pace, overnight stops and symptoms of altitude sickness in advance rather than filling the evening before departure with additional excursions.

## Bolivia: lagoons, flamingos and the salt flat

In Bolivia, attention focuses on [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), other high-altitude lakes and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The route is traveled in 4×4 vehicles. Depending on the day, stops include Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, geothermal areas, Hedionda Lagoon and Cañapa Lagoon.

The high-altitude lagoons are known for their birds, including flamingos. Individual programs mention them near the water, but **the time and place of an actual sighting depend on natural conditions**. Warm clothing layers and optical equipment are useful for bird photography; do not expect birds to be standing by the roadside when the group arrives.

This natural stage requires more preparation than a walk through Iguazu's park. Some roads are unpaved, the air is drier and temperatures change sharply over the day. Much of the experience consists of stops and driving across the plateau; the tour should not be regarded as a multi-day walking trek.

## Peru: Titicaca, the Andes and the boundary between nature and culture

After Bolivia, the routes pass through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and continue to Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The setting offers mountains, high altitude and walks, but many days focus on cultural sites: the Uros Islands, Inca monuments and historic neighborhoods.

For travelers particularly interested in birds and wildlife, it is important to distinguish **a natural area from a thematic wildlife-watching excursion**. Visiting the floating Uros Islands primarily introduces local traditions. Machu Picchu is an archaeological site amid mountains, not a specialized wildlife observation program.

On the longer [eight-country journey across South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), Ecuador's Galápagos Islands come after Peru. There, marine excursions offer opportunities to observe birds, iguanas and sea lions: one of the day's alternative programs is chosen, not both. This is a separate stage outside the four countries named in the title.

## How to choose among multi-country programs

For waterfalls, the Andes, Titicaca and Machu Picchu, compare the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) with the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). Both primarily feature natural landscapes and cultural monuments; neither advertises special excursions devoted to watching wild animals.

The broadest geography belongs to the 32-day itinerary, which continues through Ecuador and Colombia after the Andean stage. It covers more natural regions but requires considerably more travel. Comparing durations and actual stops is more useful than counting countries in the title.

Below is the 32-day itinerary, which includes the Galápagos after Peru and one of two alternative marine excursions. Scenic itineraries without a standalone wildlife program appear in the [nature travel selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_chile_peru/interests/nature/). Wildlife encounters may occur outside the four countries named in this selection.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If Bolivian lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat and natural landscapes interest you, start with [nature tours through Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/). For trips with scheduled wildlife observations, use the [multi-country “Wildlife and Safaris” catalog](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## Weather, roads and time for observations

Iguazu is humid, while the Bolivian plateau is dry and can be cold even after a warm day. In Peru, changing weather is compounded by altitude and long ground transfers. It makes sense to pack separate light clothing for warm stops, insulation for the highlands and protection from rain. Time spent crossing the Chile–Bolivia and Bolivia–Peru borders should count as part of the journey, not as excursion time.

We help select a program based on your preferred natural area, coordinate the order of stops, flights and ground transfers, and check where wildlife observation is actually scheduled rather than general sightseeing. Entry and transit conditions for your citizenship and the current rules of specific parks are checked separately before departure.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife watching in the four countries

### Does the trip guarantee a flamingo sighting in Bolivia?

No. In the wild, sightings depend on the season, weather and where the birds are on the day the lagoon is visited. The program confirms the route to natural sites, but not every animal encounter.

### Can I see Iguazu without entering Brazil?

The Argentine side is accessible as a separate natural attraction. But the available tours in this selection also include Brazil, so review the complete country list when choosing a ready-made itinerary.

### Is a separate wildlife-watching excursion included in Peru?

Our multi-country itineraries focus on Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu during the Peruvian stage. Dedicated wildlife observation should not be inferred from the tour's general thematic label.

### Which is harder: Iguazu or the Bolivian stage?

The standard Iguazu walkways mainly require comfortable shoes and time to walk. The Bolivian off-road route adds considerable altitude, cold, dry air and long journeys on unpaved roads.

## Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay: which itineraries are available?

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which all four countries form part of the main route. There are currently two distinct options:

- A [20-day group tour across six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), traveling from Rio and Iguazu to Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Santiago, the Atacama, Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu. The journey ends after Peru.
- A [32-day tour across eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) that follows a similar southern Andean route but continues through Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and several cities in Colombia.

**Neither ready-made itinerary is limited to the four selected countries.** Both also include Brazil and Peru. This filter helps compare journeys with the geography you want, but it does not replace reading the complete country list, daily itinerary and included services.

An important difference is that the 20-day trip is a group tour, while the 32-day trip combines group and individual excursions in different sections. This does not mean the entire longer journey has a personal guide or private transport: the format must be checked day by day.

## Argentina and Uruguay: the capital, tango and a ferry across the Río de la Plata

After the Brazilian stage, travelers visit [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The itinerary includes sightseeing, central neighborhoods and an evening tango show with dinner. If Argentine culture is a priority, check the guide's language and whether the specific evening event is included in your chosen version.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited from Buenos Aires **in a single day**. The morning includes a port transfer and ferry, followed by a sightseeing tour of Uruguay's capital and free time. The group returns by ferry to Argentina in the evening. This provides a convenient way to add another capital, but these programs do not include several days of seaside relaxation in Uruguay.

During the excursion, visitors can discover the [Port of Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) and the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/). Bear in mind that the described itineraries fly onward to Chile **from Buenos Aires**, not Montevideo. This affects luggage arrangements and subsequent flight connections.

Crossing the border by water requires checking passport rules in both directions. If multiple entries into Argentina matter for your nationality, confirm this before purchasing tickets.

## Chile: a city day and preparation for the Altiplano

From Buenos Aires, the journey moves to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A sightseeing tour covers the center and historic buildings, followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

The main role of Chile in both itineraries is the transition to high-altitude natural landscapes. The Atacama is the starting point for travel into Bolivia. The next section runs in off-road vehicles through high-altitude lagoons and thermal areas. This is not a tour of Chilean Patagonia: glaciers and multi-day national-park treks should not be added to expectations merely because Chile is associated with them.

An evening astronomy excursion using telescopes in the Atacama is offered separately. It cannot be treated as included in the price unless the selected tour specifically says so.

Chile has rules for declaring animal and plant products brought into the country. On a long journey with multiple borders, check the contents of your luggage in advance and do not transport food from a previous country without verifying the rules.

## Bolivia: the most challenging road stage

From San Pedro de Atacama, travelers enter Bolivia. The route uses 4×4 jeeps and visits Laguna Verde, the Sol de Mañana geyser area, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and other high-altitude lakes before reaching the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

In both programs, this is more than a brief photo stop. The route includes an overnight stay near the desert, several long road sections and visits to salt flats. Uyuni and La Paz follow, then onward travel toward Peru via Tiwanaku and Lake Titicaca.

### Altitude matters more to the choice than hotel category

Roads in southwestern Bolivia climb above 4,000 m, where headaches, poor sleep and other symptoms of altitude sickness are possible. Traveling by jeep does not protect against the effects of elevation. Before booking, discuss your individual risks with a physician and check that insurance covers the actual altitudes.

The demands come not only from visiting Uyuni but also from changes in altitude after lowland cities, overnight stays on the Altiplano and further travel toward La Paz and Puno. Anyone needing a gentler acclimatization schedule may require different timing and stops, to be arranged separately.

Clothing suited to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) will not replace warm layers for early departures and high-altitude nights. Pack layers, closed-toe footwear, sun protection and a way to keep essential items accessible during transfers.

## Twenty or thirty-two days: how the ending differs

Both programs visit [Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) after Bolivia. The choice is therefore not simply about having time to see major Inca sites: they feature in both itineraries.

| Option | After Peru |
|---|---|
| 20 days | Journey ends in Lima |
| 32 days | Ecuador and Colombia |

On the longer route, Quito, the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), Guayaquil, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá follow Lima. These add marine excursions, flights and city tours. The 20-day program cannot be extended by simply adding a few hotel nights: its next stage would have to be organized from scratch.

If vacation time is limited, the 20-day option lets you finish after an extensive introduction to six countries. If you want to travel onward from the Andes to oceanic islands and Colombian cities, compare the 32-day itinerary and its overall transport schedule. The longer tour requires not only a larger budget but also comfort with repeated changes in climate and accommodation.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Money, documents and booking

Argentina and Uruguay use different pesos, Chile has its own peso, and Bolivia uses the boliviano. The available tours also include Brazil and Peru, while the 32-day version adds Ecuador and Colombia. Budget planning must account for all countries, not only the four named in the title. Check your specific bank card and cash-withdrawal options by country and issuing bank; universal acceptance of dollars or cards cannot be promised.

Compare the inclusions of each tour: accommodation type, domestic flights, excursions, tickets, meals, guide languages and optional events. Comparing only two minimum prices without accounting for duration and the number of countries would be misleading. The group and individual elements of the 32-day program also need to be read separately.

Visa rules depend on nationality, the actual route and travel dates. These programs require checks for entry into Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru, plus the extra countries in the longer option and countries used for transit connections. We help coordinate the sequence of documents and transport, while the relevant government authorities determine actual permission to enter.

## Choosing a journey according to your priorities

If your main dream is the Altiplano lagoons and Uyuni, compare the days between the [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/) and the elevations of overnight stops. If Buenos Aires and Uruguay interest you without the demanding highland stage, explore the [Argentina and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_uruguay/). For a trip focused on two Andean countries, consider the [Bolivia and Chile selection](/multi-country/bolivia_chile/).

The extended 20- and 32-day programs are particularly appealing to travelers wishing to combine several regions in one trip. Nevertheless, pace, accommodation and the agreed excursions are determined by each specific tour. Traveling strictly through Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia would require a new itinerary with different flights and overnight stays.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay tours

### Is there a ready-made trip covering only the four countries?

We offer two programs, but both also include Brazil and Peru. The longer one additionally visits Ecuador and Colombia. A four-country option would require a separate redesign of the route.

### Do travelers stay overnight in Uruguay?

In the confirmed programs, Montevideo is a day trip from Buenos Aires with a return ferry. No additional overnight stay is specified.

### Which part is most physically demanding?

The high-altitude off-road journey through Bolivia and the subsequent trip via Titicaca. Preparation needs to account for altitude, health, rest and insurance conditions.

### How does the 32-day tour differ from the 20-day tour?

After the common journey through Peru, it continues to Ecuador, including the Galápagos, and Colombia. The overall scope, number of domestic flights and budget are different.

## Where the adventures are on the current routes, and where city tours take over

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [20-day tour of six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). “Adventure” is a secondary theme on both tours. The most active stage of this four-country combination lies **between Chile and Bolivia**: first [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), then a two-day off-road drive through the Bolivian highlands.

In Argentina, the itineraries visit [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/); in Uruguay, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). These stages involve city sightseeing and a ferry trip rather than trekking. The distinction helps travelers choose without expecting the same physical or sporting demands in every country.

## Argentina and Uruguay: a pause before the Andes

On both tours, travelers reach Buenos Aires after visiting the Argentine side of Iguazu. Excursions through historic districts and an evening of tango make for a day without off-road driving or mountain travel. The following day, the group takes a ferry to Montevideo and returns to Argentina.

The ferry excursion involves an early start, an international border crossing and a same-day return. Neither tour, however, includes sporting activities in Uruguay. Beach hikes, kayaking on the Río de la Plata or independent walks through Uruguay's nature reserves should not be added to the itinerary by default.

After these stops, travelers fly to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). This city stage comes before the plateau journey and offers a chance to prepare for changing climates.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as the gateway to high altitude

From Santiago, participants fly to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). On both itineraries, this day is associated with acclimatization before Uyuni. An evening astronomy excursion with telescopes is offered optionally, but **costs extra** and depends on observing conditions.

Do not attribute every famous Atacama activity to these tours. The route does not include a separate ascent of Licancabur Volcano, a multi-day walking trek or mountain biking. The adventure stage begins with the border crossing and the jeep trip through Bolivia.

## Bolivia: two days in 4×4 vehicles

After crossing from Chile into Bolivia, the route travels through [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques, the Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Other high-altitude lagoons follow, then Chiguana, the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/).

The main challenge is not so much the distance walked as lengthy travel at high altitude, changes in temperature and the limited comfort of the expedition stage. The program includes an overnight stay at an expedition-style hotel in the desert. For travelers with no previous high-altitude experience, this matters more than a simple label such as “easy” or “difficult excursion.”

The route climbs above 4,000 meters, where altitude sickness is a risk. Before traveling, discuss medical contraindications with a doctor, allow time to adapt, pack warm clothes and be cautious with exertion. Such measures cannot be replaced by assuming that traveling in a jeep eliminates the effects of altitude.

## Choosing clothing and equipment for the weather

Conditions in Buenos Aires, Montevideo and high-altitude Bolivia are substantially different. Ordinary comfortable shoes are useful for city days. The off-road route requires warm layers and protection from sun, wind and dry air. Packing should be guided by **the most demanding stage**, not the weather in the departure city.

Uyuni changes with rainfall: the salt flat may look like a dry white plain or be covered with water. A mirror-like surface cannot be promised on every date. Weather can also affect individual sections of the drive across the plateau. Allowing extra time for transport is important when planning connections after the Bolivian stage.

## Why these four countries do not describe the entire route

Both itineraries include Brazil before Argentina and Peru after Bolivia. Cultural days in Rio, nature excursions on both sides of Iguazu and a visit to Machu Picchu are part of the full journey, even though these countries do not appear in the selected four-country filter.

The [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues to Ecuador and Colombia, while the [20-day option](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) ends in Peru. The difference lies in overall duration and geography, not in the Bolivian off-road stage turning into a different sporting product on the longer tour.
